title: B1-14 · The diptotes: names that do not take the tanwīn

blocks.text: B1-14 · The diptotes: names that do not take the tanwīn
Lesson overview

Why is it said? ⁧مِنْ مِصْرَ⁩ and not ⁧مِنْ مِصْرٍ⁩ , ⁧فِي مَدَارِسَ كَثِيرَةٍ⁩ and not ⁧فِي مَدَارِسٍ⁩ , ⁧مَعَ أَحْمَدَ⁩ and not ⁧مَعَ أَحْمَدٍ⁩ ? Why ⁧مِصْر⁩ , ⁧مَدَارِس⁩ and ⁧أَحْمَد⁩ are diptotic ( ⁧المَمْنُوعُ مِنَ الصَّرْفِ⁩ , are prevented from complete declension ,): they do not take the tanwīn and the genitive have a. You meet them from the first unit; now learn to recognize them, so as to read out loud with the right desinences proper names, plural and adjectives. It's the last unit on the module. B1.2. A week.

rows: 6–7 hours · one week (week 122), plus the EGY track

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Grammar G54, script for speech synthesis, session with tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. decline a diptoto: -u to the name, -a to the accusative and genitive, without tanwīn;
2. recognizing the four great groups of diptotes: own names, adjectives, plural tratti, words in ⁧ـَاء⁩ ;
3. know when a diptoto returns to decline normally (with the article and in iḍāfa);
4. distinguish plural diptotes ( ⁧مَدَارِسُ⁩ , ⁧وُزَرَاءُ⁩ ) from normal ( ⁧كُتُبٌ⁩ , ⁧طُلَّابٌ⁩ );
5. read texts with their own names, cities and countries with correct desinences.

2. How to decline a diptoto
genitive ⁧مَدَارِسَكِتَابٍ⁩
Two differences: nothing tanwīn , and genitive equals the accusative (-a).
⁧دَرَسْتُ فِي مَدَارِسَ كَثِيرَةٍ.⁩ Genitive (with a!)
The adjective that follows the diptotum is normally declined, with its tanwīn: ⁧مَدَارِسَ كَثِيرَةٍ.⁩
3. The proper names

rows: female names (by meaning or by the ⁧ة⁩ )
names of countries and cities, almost all

blocks.text: Arab male names of three letters without ⁧ة⁩ are normal: ⁧مُحَمَّدٌ⁩ , ⁧عَلِيٌّ⁩ , ⁧كَرِيمٌ⁩ , ⁧سَعِيدٌ⁩ : ⁧مَعَ مُحَمَّدٍ⁩ , ⁧مَعَ كَرِيمٍ⁩ . Among the names of countries some are triptotes because Arabs and male: ⁧العِرَاقُ⁩ , ⁧اليَمَنُ⁩ , ⁧السُّودَانُ⁩ (with the article, therefore normal). Names ending in long vowel ( ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ , ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ , ⁧مِيلَانُو⁩ , ⁧رُومَا⁩ ) show no desinence.
4. Adjectives
Examples: ⁧اِشْتَرَيْتُ قَمِيصًا أَحْمَرَ⁩ I bought a red shirt. ⁧فِي سَيَّارَةٍ حَمْرَاءَ⁩ In a red car: ⁧يَسْكُنُ فِي بَيْتٍ أَكْبَرَ⁩ “lives in a larger house”.
5. The plural plurality of plurality

Golden rule: a plural over is diptototo if, after the ā, has two syllables (or a syllable with long vowel): ⁧مَفَاعِلُ⁩ , ⁧مَفَاعِيلُ⁩ , ⁧فَوَاعِلُ⁩ , ⁧فَعَائِلُ⁩ . And the plurals are diptotic in ⁧ـَاءُ⁩ : ⁧أَفْعِلَاءُ⁩ , ⁧فُعَلَاءُ⁩ .
⁧وُزَرَاءُفُعَلَاءُ⁩ ⁧شُعَرَاءُ⁩ · ⁧زُمَلَاءُ⁩ · ⁧عُلَمَاءُ⁩ · ministers · scientists · colleagues · poets
exception ⁧أَشْيَاءُ⁩ things (diptoto even if it has the scheme ⁧أَفْعَال⁩ )

The normal plurals are all the others: ⁧كُتُبٌ⁩ , ⁧طُلَّابٌ⁩ , ⁧رِجَالٌ⁩ , ⁧أَوْلَادٌ⁩ , ⁧بُيُوتٌ⁩ , ⁧أَسْمَاءٌ⁩ : ⁧فِي كُتُبٍ كَثِيرَةٍ⁩ , ⁧مَعَ رِجَالٍ.⁩ Defective diptotes ( ⁧مَقَاهٍ⁩ , ⁧مَبَانٍ⁩ , B1-07) follow the declension of defects: ⁧مَقَاهٍ⁩ (Nom., Jan.), ⁧مَقَاهِيَ⁩ (a.k.a.),
⁧المَقَاهِي⁩ .
6. When the diptototo is declined normally
A diptototo returns triptototo (with kasra al genitivo) in two cases:
1. with the article: ⁧فِي المَدَارِسِ⁩ , ⁧مَعَ الأَصْدِقَاءِ⁩ , ⁧فِي السَّيَّارَةِ الحَمْرَاءِ⁩ ;
2. as the first term of aiḍāfa: ⁧فِي مَدَارِسِ المَدِينَةِ⁩ , ⁧مَعَ أَصْدِقَائِي⁩ , ⁧فِي أَجْمَلِ مَدِينَةٍ.⁩
The tanwīn but never returns, because with the article and in iḍāfa on tanwīn He's not there anyway.

8. Pronunciation

Reading their own names. The tutor reads a list of prepositioned sentences + own name ( ⁧مِنْ مِصْرَ⁩ , ⁧إِلَى بَيْرُوتَ⁩ , ⁧مَعَ أَحْمَدَ⁩ , ⁧فِي بَغْدَادَ⁩ , ⁧عَنْ فَاطِمَةَ⁩ ); repeat by making the a feel. Then alternates with normal names ( ⁧مَعَ مُحَمَّدٍ⁩ , ⁧مَعَ كَرِيمٍ⁩ ). Pause. At the end of the sentence the diptototo loses the vowel as every name: ...ilā bārīs. The difference can only be heard inside the sentence.
